title: Prince William Gets a Bollywood Welcome at Karan Johar's Dharma Productions
excerpt: Dancers performed ‘Shava Shava’ from Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham as Karan Johar, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan hosted the Prince of Wales on the final morning of his Mumbai visit.
body:
• Prince William was welcomed to Dharma Productions in Mumbai on Wednesday with a live performance of ‘Shava Shava’ from the Hindi film Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, hosted by Karan Johar with Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan.
  • Invited to join the dancers, the prince declined with a laugh: “Maybe next time.”
  • The studio visit closed the Mumbai leg of the royal couple's three-day India tour for the Earthshot Prize, before their meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi.
  • For diaspora audiences, the stop underlined Bollywood's British connection: K3G was partly filmed in Britain and completes 25 years this December.

Prince William got Bollywood's signature welcome on Wednesday when dancers performed ‘Shava Shava’ at the entrance of Dharma Productions in Mumbai, recreating the celebration number from the 2001 Hindi film Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham in traditional outfits as the Prince of Wales watched. Filmmaker Karan Johar, Dharma's executive director, welcomed him alongside Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan, ANI reported.

William described the routine as “amazing” and “brilliant.” When the dancers invited him to join in, he laughed and replied, “Maybe next time,” and encouraged Johar to demonstrate his own moves instead: “I won't hold you back,” he joked, according to Internewscast's report of the visit.

"Maybe next time."

— Prince William, declining an invitation to join the Shava Shava dancers

Inside the studio

Inside Dharma's flower-filled offices, where high tea had been laid out, William heard about Bollywood's long connection with Britain. He met Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan for a discussion about the Indian film industry, asking how often they worked in Britain and where they filmed; the actors said they visit London around four times a year and have used locations such as the British Museum to introduce British landmarks to Indian audiences. As president of the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA), the prince's studio stop was also framed as a look at closer cooperation between the two countries' creative industries. After the conversation he toured the offices as employees gathered on balconies to watch, and posed for a photograph on a floor decorated with purple flowers and candles.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=_ETVw6okPsQ

The choice of song was deliberate. Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, known as K3G, remains one of Dharma's most recognisable films — a lavish family drama partly filmed in Britain that completes 25 years this December, and whose music is still a fixture at celebrations and dance floors.

The final morning of the Mumbai leg

Earlier on Wednesday, William and Catherine visited the Chanakya School of Craft in Lower Parel, an engagement focused on sustainable textiles, where they tried on shawls and bangles and tried block printing. The school trains women from underserved communities in traditional embroidery and textile techniques; more than 1,400 women artisans have been trained so far.

The couple's three-day visit was built around the Earthshot Prize, the environmental award William founded in 2020. They attended the awards ceremony in Mumbai on Tuesday evening — five winners, including India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, took £1 million each — and William drove an electric three-wheeler built by Mahindra Last Mile Mobility at Bandra Reclamation Garden with the prize's 15 finalists. The tour is the couple's first joint visit to India since 2016, and Catherine's first joint overseas tour with William since 2022. From Mumbai they travelled to New Delhi for a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Our earlier coverage followed the tour's opening: Prince William opened the visit in a handloom jacket woven in West Bengal.

How to follow the tour

The Delhi meeting with Prime Minister Modi closes the India tour. Kensington Palace's official Flickr account shared the pictures from the Dharma visit, and the Earthshot Prize ceremony's streaming availability was set out in our awards coverage linked above.
